catalog.biasAlertTitle: Technical Note on Data and Source Confounding (ADR 0005)
catalog.biasAlertText: All 177 COVID-19 radiographs originate from adult cohorts (Cohen and Figure1), while pneumonia and normal images originate from pediatric cohorts (Kermany). Consequently, computed difficulty partly reflects demographic and imaging equipment domain shift. A quota cap of up to 500 images per class is enforced to prevent bucket starvation.

education.title: Educational Guide & Learning Cycle
education.subtitle: Understanding adaptive training, diagnostic error extraction, and clinical differential signs
education.disclaimerText: This platform is exclusively a web-based educational training tool for radiology trainees and residents. System outputs and AI analyses do not constitute clinical diagnoses and must never be used for treatment decisions in real patients.
education.cycleTitle: How Does the Adaptive Learning Cycle Work?
education.cycleSubtitle: A 4-step intelligent question allocation process tailored to your individual weaknesses
education.cycleStep1Desc: The first test offers a balanced distribution of diagnostic classes. Subsequent tests are dynamically personalized based on your past performance.
education.cycleStep2Desc: The adaptive engine computes false-positive (FPR) and false-negative (FNR) error rates across all three disease classes (COVID-19, pneumonia, normal).
education.cycleStep3Desc: Subsequent test questions are weighted more heavily toward the disease classes and difficulty tiers where you made the most errors.
education.cycleStep4Desc: Through focused practice on frequent confusion pairs, diagnostic precision is reinforced until reaching the 80% mastery threshold across all classes.
education.metricsTitle: Guide to Interpreting Report Error Metrics
education.metricsSubtitle: Understanding false positive and false negative concepts in plain terms
education.fpDesc: Occurs when a radiograph that does not contain a specific condition is mistakenly diagnosed as that condition (e.g., misclassifying a normal scan as COVID-19).
education.fnDesc: Occurs when pathology is present in the radiograph, but you fail to detect it or misidentify it as normal (e.g., missing pneumonia consolidation).
education.classesSubtitle: Directly grounded in the approved system knowledge base (apps/api/src/modules/llm/kb)
education.covid19Desc: Typical COVID-19 findings on chest radiography include bilateral alveolar opacities, predominantly peripheral and in the lower lung zones. Ground-glass opacities (GGO) and/or consolidation are common. Pleural effusion and mediastinal lymphadenopathy are unusual, and initial chest radiographs may be normal. Definitive diagnosis requires laboratory testing and clinical correlation.
education.pneumoniaDesc: Bacterial pneumonia typically presents as focal lobar or segmental consolidation with air bronchograms and may be accompanied by parapneumonic effusion. In contrast, viral or atypical pneumonias more often present with peribronchial thickening, interstitial patterns, patchy opacities, and lung hyperinflation. Pneumonia sub-types are not differentiated in this diagnostic system.
education.normalDesc: A normal chest radiograph features clear lung fields, sharp costophrenic angles, age-appropriate cardiac and mediastinal contours, without any focal opacities or pleural effusions.
